articles.title: TEA 2025 Attendance Report: World's Top 25 Theme Parks Flatline on Visitation
articles.summary: The Themed Entertainment Association's annual Index reveals that attendance at the world's 25 leading theme parks was essentially flat in 2025. For FEC operators and investors, this macro-level stagnation signals a competitive consumer leisure market where differentiation and experience quality are critical. Understanding where the big parks are losing ground can help FEC operators identify whitespace opportunities.

articles.title: Intercard Unveils OmniRay Cashless Readers at IAAPA Expo 2026
articles.summary: Cashless technology pioneer Intercard will debut its next-generation OmniRay Readers at IAAPA Expo in Orlando this November, designed specifically to address economic headwinds facing amusement operators. The new readers include features requested directly by operators in the field. FEC operators attending IAAPA should prioritize this booth visit, as cashless payment infrastructure is a core revenue and operational efficiency driver.

articles.title: ESAC Outlines 2027 FEC Design Trends Using Shanghai WUNPARK as Case Study
articles.summary: ESAC has published analysis drawing on the Shanghai WUNPARK project to identify key FEC design trends heading into 2027, with a focus on shifting from attraction-mix venues to social destinations. The piece addresses how operators can rethink layout, programming, and guest flow to encourage longer dwell times and repeat visits. This is essential reading for anyone planning a new FEC build or major renovation.

articles.title: Merlin Entertainments to Replace Accessible Queuing System with Virtual Queue App in 2027
articles.summary: Merlin Entertainments is rolling out a new virtual queue system for its Ride Access Pass program in 2027, replacing the current system with a smartphone app that reduces physical queue time for guests with disabilities. For FEC operators, this signals a broader industry shift toward app-based accessibility accommodations that reduce friction for guests with hidden disabilities. Early adopters of similar systems in FEC settings can gain a competitive edge in inclusivity.

articles.title: New Greek FEC Selects Sacoa Cashless System for Full-Venue Deployment
articles.summary: A newly opened FEC in Greece has chosen Sacoa's cashless platform as its core payment and game management system, highlighting continued international growth for cashless technology providers in the FEC sector. The adoption reflects a global trend of new FEC builds defaulting to cashless-first infrastructure from day one. Operators evaluating or upgrading payment systems should take note of Sacoa's expanding footprint.

articles.title: LEVEL99 Puzzle-Based Entertainment Venue Sets Opening Date in West Hartford, CT
articles.summary: LEVEL99, the innovative challenge-based entertainment concept featuring dozens of physical puzzle rooms and competitive activities, has announced its opening date in West Hartford, Connecticut. The brand's continued expansion into new markets underscores strong consumer demand for adult-oriented active entertainment. FEC operators should monitor LEVEL99's format as a benchmark for skill-based, non-traditional entertainment design.

articles.title: Launch Entertainment Center Opens Large-Scale Venue in Pensacola, Florida
articles.summary: A new large-format Launch entertainment center has opened in Pensacola, bringing a mix of trampoline parks, attractions, and family entertainment to the market. The opening adds to Launch's growing national footprint and intensifies competition in the indoor active entertainment space. FEC operators in the region and those tracking the trampoline park sector should note the scale and attraction mix of this new location.

articles.title: Construction Underway on Two New Hello Park Locations
articles.summary: Construction has begun on two new Hello Park indoor entertainment locations, signaling continued investment and expansion in the branded FEC space. Hello Park's growth reflects sustained capital interest in multi-attraction indoor entertainment concepts. Operators and investors tracking the competitive landscape should watch this brand's development pipeline.

articles.title: Premiere Cinemas Anchors Major FEC Expansion at South Plains Mall in Lubbock
articles.summary: Premiere Cinemas is expanding at South Plains Mall with a large new family entertainment center, illustrating the growing trend of cinema operators broadening into multi-attraction FEC formats to drive traffic and revenue. This mall-anchored model combines the draw of a movie theater with FEC amenities to maximize dwell time. Operators and developers exploring mall-based FEC opportunities will find this a timely case study.

articles.title: Complete Sports and Management India Wins Two New FEC Projects
articles.summary: India-listed Complete Sports and Management India (CSML) has announced it has secured contracts for two new family entertainment center projects, reflecting accelerating FEC investment in the Indian market. The wins point to growing international demand for FEC development expertise and purpose-built entertainment infrastructure. Suppliers and investors with global ambitions should track the South Asian FEC pipeline closely.

articles.title: Accesso Intelligence Launches AI-Powered Library of 100+ Decision Skills for Attractions Operators
articles.summary: Accesso has introduced a library of more than 100 Decision Skills within its AI platform, covering areas including operations, guest experience, membership, finance, marketing, and retail. The tool is designed to give attractions operators data-driven guidance across virtually every business function. FEC operators using accesso's platform should evaluate how these AI-driven insights can reduce guesswork in day-to-day decision-making.

articles.title: Six Flags Expands Holiday Programming Across 11 Parks for 2026 Season
articles.summary: Six Flags Entertainment Corporation is growing its 2026 holiday season with two new events added to its roster, bringing festive programming to 11 theme parks across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, plus resort getaway offerings. The expansion reinforces seasonal event programming as a key revenue driver for large regional park operators. FEC operators can benchmark Six Flags' holiday activation scale when planning their own seasonal events.

articles.title: Wake The Tiger Opens 'Absurd City' — 80,000 Sq Ft Immersive Attraction Inside Westfield London
articles.summary: Wake The Tiger has opened Absurd City at Westfield London, now the largest single leisure tenant in the shopping center at 80,000 square feet. The opening exemplifies the retailtainment trend, with mall operator URW dedicating nearly 650,000 square feet across two London centers to leisure and entertainment to increase dwell time. FEC developers eyeing mall-based locations should study this model as a leading example of large-format immersive entertainment in retail environments.

articles.title: What Mixed-Use Developers Can Learn from Theme Park Design Principles
articles.summary: Architecture firm BRPH argues that successful mixed-use destinations require the same integrated master planning approach used in themed entertainment, including attention to pedestrian circulation, sensory design, and emotional connection. The piece draws on experience across theme parks, civic architecture, and urban planning to offer practical lessons for placemaking. FEC operators and developers involved in mixed-use or entertainment district projects will find actionable frameworks here.

articles.title: Monster Mini Golf Partners with Special Olympics for November Fundraising Campaign Across 43 Locations
articles.summary: Monster Mini Golf has launched a month-long fundraising initiative with Special Olympics, giving guests at all 43 of its North American locations the chance to donate at point of sale throughout November. The campaign demonstrates how FEC chains can leverage their scale for cause marketing, which builds community goodwill and can drive incremental traffic. Operators looking for socially impactful seasonal programming ideas should take note of this model.

articles.title: 'Masha and the Three Bears' IP Enters FEC Space with First Branded Entertainment Center
articles.summary: The popular children's IP 'Masha and the Three Bears' is launching its first family entertainment center, bringing a licensed character brand into the FEC format for the first time. IP-driven FEC concepts continue to gain traction as operators seek differentiation and built-in brand awareness. This signals growing interest from media IP holders in the physical entertainment venue space.

articles.title: First Permanent U.S. teamLab Museum to Open at Southern California's OCVIBE Development
articles.summary: Digital art collective teamLab will open its first permanent U.S. museum as part of the OCVIBE mixed-use entertainment development in Southern California, adding a high-profile immersive attraction anchor to the project. teamLab's immersive digital art environments have drawn large audiences internationally and represent a growing category of experience-led entertainment. FEC operators and developers should monitor this format's U.S. rollout as it validates consumer appetite for premium immersive venues.

articles.title: Candy Land Branded Retail-Entertainment Store Opening in New York City This November
articles.summary: A Candy Land store based on Hasbro's iconic board game is opening adjacent to the New York Hilton Midtown, translating the beloved IP into a real-life candy and entertainment experience. The concept is part of a broader wave of board game and toy IP activations in physical retail-entertainment. FEC operators exploring IP licensing and pop-up experience models will find this a relevant reference point.

articles.title: Wisconsin Pub Installs Indoor Golf Simulators to Drive Winter Revenue
articles.summary: A bar in Beloit, Wisconsin has added golf simulators to its offering to capture revenue during the slower winter months, reflecting the rapid spread of simulator-based entertainment into hospitality venues. This grassroots adoption of golf sim technology by non-dedicated entertainment venues signals intensifying competition for FEC operators in the casual gaming space. Operators running simulator bays or considering adding them should track how hospitality venues are packaging and pricing the experience.

articles.title: New Owner Revives Closed Bowling Alley, Betting on Nostalgia and Community Ties
articles.summary: A shuttered bowling alley in Ozaukee County, Wisconsin is being reborn under new ownership, with the operator citing community nostalgia and demand for local social entertainment as the driving motivation. The story is representative of a broader trend of independent operators acquiring and relaunching legacy bowling venues. FEC operators and investors interested in bowling acquisitions will find this a useful grassroots case study.

articles.title: SPRK Lighting on Designing Immersive Guest Journeys Through Integrated Lighting
articles.summary: SPRK Lighting's principals discuss how lighting design must balance immersive storytelling with practical needs including wayfinding, retail support, and long-term operational costs in visitor attractions. The firm's integrated approach connects creative vision with technical delivery from early planning stages, reducing costly revisions. FEC operators planning new builds or renovations should consider how lighting design strategy affects both guest experience and operational budget.

articles.title: GoPhoto Advances Attraction Photography with Personalized Digital Backgrounds and Themed Imagery
articles.summary: GoPhoto is rolling out new capabilities that allow attraction photographers to combine digital backgrounds, themed costumes, and customized poses to create more memorable and marketable souvenir photos. The technology extends the guest experience beyond the physical attraction and creates new incremental revenue opportunities for operators. FEC operators running on-site photography programs should evaluate how GoPhoto's personalization tools could lift per-cap spending.

articles.title: Adventureland NY Adds Two New Zamperla Rides for 65th Anniversary Season
articles.summary: Adventureland in Farmingdale, New York is celebrating its 65th anniversary by adding two new Zamperla-designed rides — the Tigers Den Family Roller Coaster and the Flying Tigers — while retiring its Antique Cars attraction. The investment demonstrates how mid-size independent parks are refreshing their attraction mix to stay competitive. FEC operators and park owners planning capital expenditures will find the Zamperla family ride additions a timely reference.

articles.title: Pensacola's New Pelican Indoor Entertainment Complex Opens to Strong Interest
articles.summary: A new indoor entertainment complex called The Pelican has opened in Pensacola, Florida, offering a multi-attraction experience within a single venue. The opening adds to a growing cluster of indoor entertainment options in the Pensacola market, increasing competitive pressure on existing operators. FEC operators in the Southeast should monitor this new entrant and its attraction mix for competitive intelligence.

articles.title: Tivoli Gardens' Hikari Japanese-Themed Area Demonstrates Multi-Generational FEC Design
articles.summary: Hikari, covering more than 2,000 square meters at Tivoli Gardens in Copenhagen, is the park's largest recent themed development and blends rides, dining, art, retail, and storytelling for multi-generational appeal. The design philosophy centers on ensuring every family member finds something personally engaging while still sharing the visit as a group. FEC designers and operators can draw direct lessons from Hikari's approach to programming breadth and themed environment cohesion.

articles.title: PIXERA Multi-Projector Sync Platform Powers Czech Republic's Largest Digital Art Gallery
articles.summary: The PIXERA media server platform is keeping 19 projectors synchronized at Signal Space, a nearly 27,000-square-foot digital art gallery in the Czech Republic that opened in September 2025. The venue represents the growing category of large-format digital immersive attractions that are expanding beyond Asia into European and North American markets. FEC operators and developers considering immersive digital art venue formats should understand the AV infrastructure requirements this scale demands.
